## Summary

I changed the `customerCode` format from `'<LAST3>-<NNNN>'` to `'<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>'` with a per-city sequence, in `src/main/java/.../rest/function/owner/AssignCustomerCode.java`:

- **CITY3** — upper-cased first three letters of `city`
- **LAST3** — upper-cased first three letters of `lastName`
- **NNNN** — a per-city 4-digit zero-padded sequence, computed as one more than the number of owners already in that city (filtering `findAll()` by city, case-insensitively), preserving the "count-before-save so consecutive creates get consecutive numbers" behavior — now scoped per city.

The **membership number** (`'<customerCode>-M<YY>'`) is automatically rebuilt on the new format because `AssignMembershipNumber` reads `owner.getCustomerCode()` at runtime; I updated its javadoc example (`SYD-SMI-0007-M26`) to match. No other values are derived from `customerCode`.

The full suite (all 26 acceptance tests across Cp01–Cp16) is green, including the two directly targeting this change — `Cp09` (per-city consecutive sequence, `SYD-ALP-`/`SYD-BRA-`) and `Cp14` (membership number over the new code) — plus `Cp16` (format regex `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}`).
